oneSentenceSummary: Big tech’s embrace of agentic commerce tools paradoxically intensifies their platform lock-in ambitions, even as they promote the illusion of merchant empowerment and choice.
editorialTake:
AI agents are not liberating commerce, they are corralling it. Shopify’s move to embed agentic storefronts directly inside ChatGPT, just as Amazon expands its Shop Direct program to let customers buy across rival sites, looks like a win for merchants. But both are building new layers of dependency: Shopify’s storefronts run on OpenAI’s rails, and Amazon’s program keeps the transaction inside its own data flows, not the retailer’s.

Nvidia’s $20 billion bet on new AI chips, and AWS’s partnership with Cerebras to accelerate agent-based applications, reinforce the same logic. The more powerful the agent, the more merchants rely on proprietary infrastructure to reach and serve customers. The counterargument is that these tools offer new reach and efficiency, but the price is ceding data, margin, and direct customer access to the platforms.

Luxury and jewellery brands cannot afford to treat agentic commerce as just another channel. Every integration should be weighed against the loss of direct customer data and brand control. In the next quarter, I would audit every new AI-powered sales touchpoint for its true cost in customer ownership and brand distinctiveness.
